s022.description:
Are Black Friday deals real? Why most "discounts" are the same price you could pay any other time.
The "was" price trick, countdown clocks, and why prices often drop again after the sale.

Consumer group Which? tracked 175 products at eight big UK retailers from May 2024 to May 2025. 83% were the same price or cheaper at least once outside the Black Friday sale period. One Samsung TV cost £1,039 on Black Friday and was cheaper on 134 days in the six months after, dropping as low as £759 (about 27% less). The real test is the price history, not the percent off. Not financial advice.

Sources:
https://www.which.co.uk/policy-and-insight/article/dont-believe-the-hype-most-black-friday-deals-the-same-price-or-cheaper-at-other-times-of-the-year-which-finds-a3TbD5x5KADs

s023.description:
Fake FTC call scam: "Your phone number is linked to a crime and will be deactivated."
How the government-impersonation call moves you from a fake official to a fake police officer to a "security deposit".

On 22 Oct 2026 the US Federal Trade Commission warned about callers posing as FTC officials who say a phone in your name is running scams overseas. They read a fake badge ID, threaten to deactivate your number, transfer you to a fake police officer, ask for your ID and secrecy, then claim you're under arrest unless you pay a "security deposit". The FTC says real employees never ask for money, threats to disconnect your phone are a scam, and requests for secrecy are always a scam. Report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Sources:
https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2026/10/ftc-not-calling-deactivate-your-phone-number

Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.
#Shorts #scam #FTC
s023.comment: Has a fake agency ever called you? 👇 FTC: real staff never ask for money, never threaten to cut off your phone, and never ask you to keep it secret.

s024.description:
Why the US stopped making the penny: each one-cent coin cost almost 4 cents to make.
The end of the US penny, and why the nickel loses money too.

In 2024 the US Mint spent about 3.69 cents to make each penny. Pennies had been made since 1793. The Treasury placed its final order for penny blanks in 2025, and the last circulating pennies were struck in Philadelphia on 12 Nov 2025. The nickel costs about 13.78 cents to make and is still being produced. More than 114 billion pennies are still in circulation, and they remain legal tender.

Sources:
https://www.nbcnews.com/business/consumer/treasury-dept-winding-penny-production-rcna208522
